Crassiorem victum exposcere tertiana quā quotidianam, contra recentiores medicos.
main_text.head: CAPVT XIIII.
main_text.p: SED qualis victus febri quæ à pituita orQ tum habet conueniat hucusque dictum est. Inuestigare tamen oportet, an verum sit quod nonnulli ex nostris medicis asserunt, crassiorem victum exposcere hanc quàm tertianam simplicem: rationem ad id sumentes longiorem hanc febrem esse quàm tertianam: cunque crassities victus & eius contrarium, à distantia status sumenda sint, fit, ut morbi qui breuius finiantur magis tenuem, qui verò tardius, crassiorem victum exposcant. Præterea labores et symptomata maiora seu vehementiora, cibū magis quàm remissiora prohibere. Iis & similibus adducuntur rationibus ut phlegmatica febre crassiori victu laborantes alant, quàm tertiana. Sed eos à via recta deuiare existimo triplici ratione, duabus ab ipsa febre, tertia à morbi vtraq

page.notes: The heading "CAPVT XIIII." is printed with the Roman numeral XIIII. The first word of the chapter opens with a large initial S, read as "SED". Line "ratione, duabus ab ipsa febre" and the final word "vtraq" (utraque, with abbreviation mark) are at the foot of the text; the last line is partly cut off at the right margin. Some words in the body are doubtful due to the italic type, notably "Inuestigare", "cunque" and "crassities", and "orQ" at the end of the first line is a rendering of the initial-letter overlap and may be a misreading.
